tagline: Global leader in renewable energy infrastructure with contracted, inflation-linked cash flows
hero_kpi_rationale: Key performance indicator used by the company to assess its operating cash flows and support distributions to unitholders. FFO of $1,334 million in 2025 (+9.6% yoy) reflects organic growth, improved hydrology, and capital recycling initiatives, demonstrating the company's sustainable ability to generate returns.

kpis.name: Funds From Operations
kpis.explanation: Measures cash flows generated from operating activities, adjusted to reflect underlying economic performance and capacity to distribute to unitholders.
kpis.description: FFO is the primary metric used by the company to evaluate economic performance and determine distributions to unitholders. In 2025, FFO of $1,334 million represents an increase of $117 million compared to 2024, driven by improved hydroelectric performance, organic growth, and capital recycling gains.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in operating cash flows driven by improved hydrology and asset base expansion.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total revenues generated from renewable energy production and sales, and related services.
kpis.description: Revenue of $6,407 million in 2025 represents an increase of $531 million (+9.0%) compared to 2024, reflecting portfolio growth (acquisitions of Isagen and Neoen), inflation escalations on energy contracts, and improved hydrology at Canadian and Colombian hydropower assets, partially offset by recent asset sales.
kpis.signal: Revenue growth driven by acquisitions and inflation escalations on contracts.

kpis.name: Direct Operating Costs
kpis.explanation: Direct costs related to the operation of renewable facilities, including maintenance, operating personnel, and asset operating expenses.
kpis.description: Direct operating costs of $2,903 million in 2025 represent an increase of $323 million (+12.5%) compared to 2024, primarily attributable to additional costs from recently acquired and commissioned facilities, partially offset by recent asset sales.
kpis.signal: Cost increase in line with asset portfolio growth.

kpis.name: Interest Expense
kpis.explanation: Amount of interest paid on consolidated debt used to finance assets and operations.
kpis.description: Interest expense of $2,457 million in 2025 represents an increase of $469 million (+23.6%) compared to 2024, reflecting additional debt incurred to finance strategic acquisitions and portfolio growth. The average interest rate on non-recourse borrowings increased from 5.4% to 5.9%, partially offset by capital structure optimization and debt maturity extensions.
kpis.signal: Higher interest expense reflecting asset portfolio expansion and a higher interest rate environment.

kpis.name: Depreciation and Amortization
kpis.explanation: Allocation of the value of renewable infrastructure assets over their estimated useful life.
kpis.description: Depreciation and amortization of $2,425 million in 2025 represents an increase of $415 million (+20.6%) compared to 2024, resulting from the addition of significant assets during the year through the acquisitions of Isagen and Neoen, and the commissioning of 8 GW of new capacity.
kpis.signal: Higher depreciation reflecting the expansion of the consolidated asset base.

kpis.name: Proportionate Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Non-IFRS measure of adjusted operating profit, excluding non-recurring items and financing effects, reflecting core operating performance.
kpis.description: Proportionate Adjusted EBITDA of $2,698 million in 2025 represents an increase of $290 million (+12.0%) compared to 2024, reflecting organic growth, improved hydrology, and accretive strategic acquisitions.
kpis.signal: Robust growth in operational cash-generating capacity.

kpis.name: Installed Capacity
kpis.explanation: Total electricity generation capacity owned and operated by the company, including all hydroelectric, wind, and solar projects.
kpis.description: Total installed capacity reached 47,203 MW in 2025, an increase of 992 MW (+2.1%) compared to 2024, reflecting the delivery of 8 GW of new renewable capacity and strategic asset acquisitions, with a target of 10 GW per year by 2027.
kpis.signal: Steady expansion of the yield-generating asset base.

kpis.name: Total Energy Generation
kpis.explanation: Total electrical energy generated by all renewable production assets, measured in gigawatt-hours.
kpis.description: Actual total generation of 116,010 GWh in 2025 represents an increase of 35,168 GWh (+43.6%) compared to 2024, driven by improved hydrology in Canadian and Colombian hydropower portfolios and the addition of 8 GW of new capacity through acquisitions and internal development.
kpis.signal: Significant increase in actual generation driven by asset expansion and improved hydrological conditions.

risks.title: Dependence on energy regulation and government policies
risks.score_rationale: Core risk for renewable energy producer: Item 1A explicitly mentions FERC, PPAs, and multiple regulatory frameworks (US, Canada, Brazil, Europe). Heavy language on dependence on incentive policies (IRA). Central to business model.

risks.title: Hydrological risk and variability in energy production
risks.score_rationale: Major operational risk for hydro-wind-solar portfolio: references to LTA (long-term average), MRE (Brazil), seasonal variability. Direct impact on Adjusted EBITDA and FFO. Trend increasing with climate change.

risks.title: Geographic concentration and political risks across multiple jurisdictions
risks.score_rationale: Portfolio diversified but exposed to Brazil, Canada, US, Europe: references to LATAM Holdco, NA Holdco, Euro Holdco. Political, regulatory instability, and foreign exchange risks. Moderate language but high strategic weight.

risks.title: Dependence on Brookfield Corporation and conflicts of interest
risks.score_rationale: Brookfield is a major shareholder, service provider (Master Services Agreement, Energy Marketing Agreement), and asset manager. Multiple references to Brookfield Holders, Conflicts Protocols, Relationship Agreement. High structural conflict risk.

risks.title: Technological risks and obsolescence of energy assets
risks.score_rationale: Portfolio includes hydro, wind, solar, BESS, CSP, eFuels, RNG: rapidly evolving technologies. References to innovation and development. Moderate but rising risk with energy transition and technological disruption.

risks.title: Cybersecurity of critical energy infrastructure
risks.score_rationale: Dedicated Item 16K on Cybersecurity Risk Management and Strategy. Energy infrastructures are critical targets. Formal language indicates recognized and formalized risk. Growing threat trend.

risks.title: Credit risk and long-term debt refinancing
risks.score_rationale: Multiple debt structures (Canadian Bonds, Perpetual Notes, BRELP Preferred Units) with complex indentures. References to interest rates (CORRA, LIBOR), refinancing. High credit risk in a rising rate environment.

risks.title: Litigation and multi-jurisdictional regulatory compliance risks
risks.score_rationale: Operations in 5+ jurisdictions (Canada, US, Brazil, Europe) with complex regulatory frameworks (CBCA, ABCA, Bermuda Acts, IFRS). Risk of environmental, contractual, and tax litigation. Moderate language but significant operational weight.

ai_positioning.summary: No mention of artificial intelligence or related technologies in the provided documents. The company does not position AI as a strategic lever.
evidence: No reference to AI in the MD&A
Absence of KPIs related to AI-driven technological innovation
Exclusive focus on physical renewable infrastructure assets and operational management
